Sports.title: The secrets to stopping Lionel Messi: Schoolboy mistakes England need to avoid, how Egypt nailed it (for 79 minutes), Carlo Ancelotti's advice and why Argentina's 'dummies' are key
Sports.content:
Kieran Trippier tells a story of how Diego Simeone, his former boss at Atletico Madrid, instructed his troops on how best to prepare for the prospect of facing Lionel Messi. How do you stop the greatest player of all time? What tactics, plans or shapes? Trippier said Simeone gave his answer before the team meetings even began: ‘Pray.’ Carlo Ancelotti had a different approach. 'If you want to prepare well for a game against Messi, you have to avoid speaking about Messi,' he said. 'If you speak to your players about the skills of Messi, they will be afraid.' Messi is 39 now, yet perhaps that rule still applies. The little maestro has scored eight goals at this World Cup, more even than he managed in almost single-handedly dragging Argentina to glory in Qatar, and somehow Thomas Tuchel and England must find some answers of their own if they are to reach a first final since 1966. What’s most remarkable is teams are failing to stop a player who barely sprints, hardly even runs, and so often stands still. Messi’s average speed of 2.8mph at the World Cup is bettered by 579 other players. According to Opta, of the 46 forwards to play more than 200 minutes, Messi’s 2.7 sprints per 90 puts him dead last by a considerable margin. Lionel Messi has scored eight goals in the USA this summer, more than he's managed at any other World Cup, and he's knocking on 40 Messi’s average speed of 2.8mph at the World Cup is bettered by 579 other players

Your browser does not support iframes.

His team has reached the semi-finals, twice via extra-time, yet the 28.7 miles he’s covered along the way is bettered by 84 other players. Harry Kane, by contrast, has run more than 42 miles. And yet, still, no one can touch him. It’s as if he’s a ghost. Thankfully, for Tuchel at least, the key to stopping Messi these days is not about stopping Messi. It’s about stopping the rest of the Argentina team from creating the space for Messi to thrive. You can, almost, fulfil Ancelotti's wish: talk about everybody else instead. Because gone are the days when Messi’s team-mates could just pass to him and stand back while he dribbled past eight players. He’s nearly 40. So the entire team works to a single gameplan – get Messi on the ball unmarked in dangerous areas. The system works separately from Messi, who is unshackled and free to wander and influence. Against Switzerland in the quarter-final, Messi touched the ball more than 100 times across nearly every blade of grass of the opposition half – even taking a few inside his own. Messi's touch map against Switzerland shows how he likes to get on the ball all around the pitch One of the main ways boss Lionel Scaloni engineers space for Messi is through dummy runs from his midfielders. Scaloni packs his side with incisive central midfielders like Enzo Fernandez, Alexis Mac Allister, Rodrigo De Paul and Leandro Paredes to help build up in a narrow 4-1-3-2 formation in which Messi, nominally, is one of the strikers. As you can see from the touch map above, he rarely stays there. Argentina’s Plan A is to pack the middle corridor of the pitch and trust their passers to play cutting balls through the crowd – where opponents are so busy trying to account for all the blue-and-white shirts – to find Messi between the lines. It’s what they did for his opening goal against Algeria. Argentina play a pass through a crowded midfield into the feet of Messi for his opening goal against Algeria It’s a high-risk approach. Elliot Anderson or Declan Rice, if fit, know that if they cut out the pass, they can spring an attack. They will back themselves to do so. However, Argentina know they also have enough bodies around the ball to snuff counters out quickly. That’s why Scaloni also calls for the dummies. His midfielders make diagonal runs out wide to draw their men away from the congestion to free up, you guessed it, Messi. Early in their victory over Austria, De Paul receives the ball in his own half, a packed midfield in front of him. He plays it backwards before busting a gut to get to the touchline. Argentina midfielder Rodrigo De Paul pops the ball off backwards and then sets off for the touchline to create space The next time he receives it, he’s got chalk on his boots, a defender drawn over to him and the path to Messi is clear. De Paul has the ball out wide but has attracted an Austrian defender leaving Messi (circled) in a one-on-one situation Panicked, the Austria bodies swarm around Messi, leaving his team-mates unmarked and free for the little man to find. He does just that, of course, and Argentina win a penalty (that Messi misses). A swarm of Austrian defenders have been drawn to Messi who pops the ball off to a team-mate in space. Argentina go on to win a penalty from the move Argentina play the same trick against Algeria. De Paul, again, collects the ball inside his own half. This time, Julian Alvarez makes the run, towing his defender along for the ride while Messi shimmies the other way. In the blink of an eye, Messi has the ball in space. Julian Alvarez makes a run towards the touchline, taking an Algerian defender with him, leaving Messi free to collect the ball in the centre circle Algeria are in all sorts of trouble now. Runners either side of the defensive shape drag them out of position, torn between closing Messi down or following the cavalry. They choose the latter and make the mistake so many teams do: they forget about Messi who releases the ball to Nico Gonzalez (No 15 on the left of the attack). Algeria backpedal as Messi travels with the ball and Argentina runners pull them out of shape, allowing Messi to pass to Nico Gonzalez (No 15, on the left of the attack) Desperately trying to recover, they leave Messi (circled) who gets it back and completes his hat-trick. Messi collects the return pass from Gonzalez and completes his hat-trick The problem is that, for as slowly as Messi walks, the rest happens so quickly. Argentina average the most passes per attack of any nation at the World Cup and take the longest over them. But when the opening appears, they shift gears in a flash. Defenders must be decisive but Argentina’s plan plants enough doubt that makes split-second decisions nearly impossible. Take this moment against Switzerland (below). Fernandez has the ball and Messi drifts deeper while the Swiss camp in their box. Zeki Amdouni, No 23, considers stepping out but knows Gonzalez, over his shoulder, would be left completely unmarked for a ball to the back post. So, he stays where he is, Messi gets the ball, drops the shoulder, turns his man and rifles a shot just wide. Messi drops into space, giving the Swiss players difficult decisions to make And he can still run in behind as well as come short. At nearly 40, he can’t make darting runs all the time but he still has the nose for when to make one. He did so for his opener against Cape Verde, latching on to a long ball over the top and almost did it again late on against Switzerland. Messi shows that he can still dart in behind defenders with his opener against Cape Verde He almost repeats the trick against Switzerland in the quarter-final England have to find a way to combat it all. Make sure to cut off those thread-needle passes through the middle. Don’t be fooled by the decoys and always have a man keeping track of Messi. Whatever you do, do not take your eye off him for a second. But don’t all try to surround him either because, as Austria found out, it leaves too many others open. This is, of course, much easier said than done. So, what’s the gameplan? Should Tuchel get someone to man-mark Messi? Djed Spence, perhaps? Follow him wherever he goes? Argentina's players give Messi a lift after victory over Egypt - but they have not been carrying him during the World Cup That’s the trap Messi wants you to fall into. The more he’s marked, the deeper he drops, the more he wanders. If Spence, or even Anderson, trots after him like a dog on a lead, suddenly there’s a huge gap for someone else to fill and for Lautaro Martinez or Alvarez to exploit. Not to mention the man-marker has to sustain that concentration and discipline for 90 minutes, even 120. Egypt and Cape Verde provided the best examples of how to do it. Egypt passed him around between zones, while Cape Verde basically ignored him completely until he strolled into a dangerous zone. They both kept their compact shape, didn’t allow Argentina to play through them. In short: defend the space, not the man, and never let your shape break. Against Cape Verde, he scored early but then didn’t create a chance from open play until the 88th minute. But even that, sadly, is not foolproof. Egypt defended him so well that Messi, by the end, was pushed wide. From there, however, he set up the first goal with a cross in the 79th minute and then scored the equaliser after another ball in from the right. Against Cape Verde, Argentina scored from two of his outswinging corners. Not to worry, Big Dan Burn will be on the pitch by that stage to head them all clear. The answer to all England’s prayers.

Sports.title: Lamine Yamal dazzles and Rodri was a forcefield to help bend World Cup semi-final Spain's way - but victory over France was the story of the collective over the individual
Sports.content:
The vast stadium screen which hangs above the pitch here beamed the image of Lamine Yamal, the teenager whose thin hairband carried the number 08304. It’s the postcode for the working-class district of the Catalonian district which he calls home.

He was standing there with his teammates hearing the anthems played, looking for all the world as if he had just wandered in from that neighbourhood. But he set his nation on their way to the World Cup final on Tuesday night, winning the penalty to secure a lead from which they never looked back.

Spain dominated the midfield and choked off the supply line to France’s stellar forward line which had pitifully little chance to bring the team back.

It was a complete performance which telegraphed to Argentina and England what one of them will be up against in Sunday’s New Jersey final. Arguably the greatest Spain side we have ever seen.

Spain earned a 2-0 victory over favourites France to progress to their second World Cup final

Mikel Oyarzabal held his nerve from the spot to give Spain a deserved lead in the first half

Royal Rodri

He has been a superb presence at this World Cup and here was a performance befitting the Ballon d’Or he won in 2024. Rodri was the architect of this 2-0 win, though the Man of the Match Award – or ‘Superior Player’ as they’re calling it, again went to the wrong individual, in Pedro Porro.

Spain knew they were up against a superior attacking force than the one they possessed. But in Rodri, they had a force field who could close their midfield down.

When France began brightly, with Ousmane Dembele and Michael Olise briefly threatening, Rodri simply cut off the central passing lanes. France were chasing down blind alleys. They were slowly suffocated.

Denied the space he tends to thrive in, Olise swapped wings with Dembele in an attempt to find some. On a most wretched night for France, space simply never came.

There will be much talk of Yamal before Sunday’s final but Rodri is the one who Spain’s opponents must devise a plan for.

Rodri was the architect of Spain's victory, acting as a forcefield in the midfield to protect his defence

Mbappe chasing shadows

Mbappe was oozing self-confidence once again as he walked out here last night in France’s stylish pinstripe shirt.

It’s all well and good having a front four like theirs but it doesn’t work when there is no-one to get the ball up to them. Mbappe was unable to land a blow because France were unable to land him opportunities. There were a few fleeting chances but he could not capitalise.

When Dembele sent a gorgeous diagonal ball across 30 yards to Mbappe in the first half, Spaniards swarmed around him. When Jules Kounde fizzed a low ball into Spain’s six-yard box, Mbappe was a yard or more behind it.

His barrelling run into the box just beyond the hour for a shot which sailed narrowly wide was a rare moment of jeopardy for an untroubled Spanish back four. He was booked before the end.

Kylian Mbappe was unable to land a blow on Spain after being starved of supply

Barcola gamble fails

Didier Deschamps had selected the PSG wide man Bradley Barcola instead of Desire Doue on the left because he is a more dynamic and attacking player, seen as more likely to bring danger to Spain. But Barcola could not set this pace alight because he couldn’t operate well in such tight spaces. A cut inside brought a shot which sailed high and wide.

Doue replaced him in the hope of something better and the France contingent in this stadium cheered at the sight of him. But nothing changed. Until that half chance Barcola carved open, France’s XG had been 0.01

Olmo and Oyarzabal collectivism

It was a brutal schooling for a France side who were played off the park and Spain’s so-called lesser lights were key. Mikel Oyarzabal, the Real Sociedad player, who coolly converted the penalty Yamal won, has scored 30 goals in 60 appearances for his country - yet would admit that he is just a solid pro. He was given his Sociedad debut by David Moyes.

There were some wonderful moments from Barca’s Dani Olmo, the Spain No 10, too. An intricate one-two between Porro and Olmo, with Olmo at its apex, brought Spain’s second.

No France defender had tracked the Porro as he doubled the lead. Olmo’s backheel to Yamal in tight space almost put Spain 2-0 up before half-time, too. Lamal’s cross found Fabian Ruiz, who put ball wide.

Pedro Porro doubled the after the break after a fine move from Spain against a below-par France

Lethal Lamal

Yamal was lurking, just out of Lucas Digne’s peripheral vision, as the defender struggled to get a ball under control and though his kick at him was accidental, it was a foul, nonetheless. A justifiable penalty.

Though he didn’t dominate the game and has had a relatively quiet tournament, he was always present, putting the fear of God into the France rearguard. Tracing a path along the dead ball after collecting possession from a blocked free kick. Getting in behind on a Porro pass early in the second half.

Lucas Digne gave away a penalty after kicking Lamine Yamal as he attempted to clear the ball

Yamal will look to lead Spain to World Cup glory as Mbappe and France lick their wounds

Any excuses for France?

It didn’t help their belief that they lost William Saliba early on. The Arsenal defender seemed to jar his back as he fell awkwardly.

Nor that the player who had initially looked like France’s own sentry, Adrien Rabiot, received an early yellow card which, with Yamal to police, left created too much of a risk for him to reappear for the second half.

But this defeat will take some stomaching for a French nation who expected far more on Bastille Day.

William Saliba limped off for France in the first half with his injury a major blow

So where now for France?

They look into an uncertain future – defeated in three successive tournament semi-finals by a golden Spanish generation and looking to a new manager to help them find the way. Deschamps is stepping down. Zinedine Zidane is the overwhelming favourite to replace him.

It’s not the first time France will go home with lots of bouquets but no trophy. Michel Platini's great team of 1982 and 1986 lost back-to-back semis, too. The new manager has Olise and Doue as the new wave of talent. Hugo Etikike and Warren Zaire-Emery may also develop as stars for Les Bleus. But there is little consolation here. Spain look like they might dominate for some time to come.

France now face an uncertain future having lost three successive semi-finals by Spain

The defeat will see Didier Deschamps' era as France manager end in the third placed play-off

Lessons for England or Argentina?

Simply that it will take a monumental performance and perhaps a slice or two of luck in New Jersey to defeat Luis del Fuente’s side, which looks a more complete one than the World Cup winning squad of 2010.

They are excellent in possession and out of it. They have conceded just one goal at this tournament and were defensively strong when France came back at them near the end.

Rodri is such a force – shielding the defence and cutting off midfield supply lines. And though Spain lack the world class central striker of other nations, Yamal is a clear and present danger at all times.

Sports.title: Which Premier League star was given just 2/10 for his display against Spain? L'Equipe deliver their damning verdict on France flops after surprise World Cup exit
Sports.content:
France's World Cup stars were not spared by L'Equipe after their World Cup campaign came to an underwhelming end with a 2-0 defeat by Spain in the semi-finals.

Didier Deschamps' side had headed into the tournament as favourites to win the World Cup, with the view having only grown with free-flowing attacking performances through to the semi-finals.

France, however, came unstuck with a Mikel Oyarzabal penalty and Pedro Porro strike preventing them from reaching a third successive World Cup final.

Spain succeeded in keeping France's stellar attack, which had scored 16 goals at the tournament, at arm's length throughout the match in Dallas.

French newspaper L'Equipe were damning in their assessment of the performance as Deschamps' side were beaten in the semi-finals of a third straight tournament by Spain.

Lucas Digne was particularly highlighted by L'Equipe, with the Aston Villa full back having clumsily given away the penalty after kicking Lamine Yamal as he went to clear the ball, unaware that the Spain star was closing him down.

Kylian Mbappe was given a 3/10 rating by L'Equipe after France lost 2-0 to Spain in the World Cup semi-finals

Lucas Digne was given a 2/10 rating after giving away the penalty that led to Spain's opening goal

Ousame Dembele was also marked at 2/10 after he did 'almost everything wrong'

'Between his uncontrolled header and his foul on Lamine Yamal, he made two mistakes that resulted in a penalty,' L'Equipe wrote, while giving Digne a 2/10 rating.

'He seemed to have got back into the game before the break but his second half was marked by repeated losses of the ball and his replacement by Theo Hernandez.'

Digne was one of three players in the French team to be given a 2/10 mark, with two of their brightest stars Michael Olise and reigning Ballon d'Or Ousmane Dembele also critiqued.

'Initially on the right, then moved centrally after half an hour, nothing helped: the Ballon d'Or winner did almost everything wrong,' L'Equipe summarised Dembele's display.

'As the minutes ticked by, he gradually faded until he became almost invisible. A huge disappointment.'

The newspaper stated that after Olise had 'risen so high in previous matches, he fell very low this time.

Olise's lack of precision with several failed passes and dribbles had meant he was unable to do harm to the Spanish defence.

Captain Kylian Mbappe received a 3/10 rating for his performance, with the outlet noting that he 'often seemed very isolated' and there 'tried to do everything himself, without success'.

Didier Deschamps received a 3/10 score after his France side came up short against Spain

Dani Olmo received an 8/10 rating with the Spain star deemed to be the player of the match

No French player received a rating above the 5/10, which was given to Jules Kounde, Dayot Upamecano and Adrien Rabiot.

Rabiot was noted as having shown 'personality and a huge impact off the ball', despite the midfielder having to be substituted at half-time due to being booked in the first half.

The defeat meant Didier Deschamps' long reign as France head coach will come to an end in the third place play-off.

Deschamps, who led France to World Cup glory in 2018 and the final in 2022, was given a 3/10 rating for his management of the semi-final.

'It's hard to understand how his team could have missed the mark so completely in terms of their approach, arriving with so much confidence,' L'Equipe stated.

'The decision to replace [Desire] Doue with [Bradley] Barcola didn't pay off, and the coaching was too deferential to the established order.'

By contrast, L'Equipe highlighted several Spanish players and their head coach Luis de la Fuente for praise.

Porro and Dani Olmo were the top scoring players with 8/10 ratings, with the latter named as their player of the match.

The mark also given to De la Fuente, with the newspaper stating his team 'displayed complete control of the match' and 'never looked threatened'.

Sports.title: Man United among clubs looking at France midfielder, Leeds reach £34m agreement on Bosnia star and Arsenal eye Greece forward after Leandro Trossard seals £17m exit: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Hull in talks over Greek keeper

Hull City have opened talks with Olympiacos goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis.

The 23-year-old has been attracting attention from Brighton, Leeds United and Aston Villa.

Tzolakis has nine caps for Greece and would be competing with Jack Butland at Hull.

Mason Greenwood in at Fenerbahce

Fenerbahce have welcomed the arrival of Mason Greenwood with a social media video after they agreed a permanent deal with Marseille of around £34million.

Manchester United are due 40 per cent of the overall fee, although 20 per cent of that will go to Getafe, who took Greenwood on loan for the 2023-24 season.

As previously reported, that should work out around £10.2million.

Beklenen an geldi! Mason Greenwood Fenerbahçemizde! 🤩



Hemen izlemek için 👉 https://t.co/xjXmWlsbIP pic.twitter.com/9yalGnrkPt — Fenerbahçe SK (@Fenerbahce) July 14, 2026

Palace ponder Norgaard move

Crystal Palace are among the clubs weighing up a move for Arsenal’s Christian Norgaard, who is keen to stay in London but has interest from Saudi too.

United among clubs circling Roma's Kone

Manchester United are among a number of clubs who have checked on Roma midfielder Manu Kone.

The 25-year-old has been at the World Cup with France and his stock is rising with Roma looking to cash in.

Atletico Madrid and Arsenal have spoken to his representatives but are looking at other options too.

United want more energy in their midfield and that will be key to their next addition as they assess targets.

Aston Villa, Manchester City, Chelsea, Newcastle and potentially Liverpool are all looking at midfielders in a congested market.

Manu Kone has been playing for France at the World Cup

Leeds close to £34m Tarik

Leeds have reached a provisional agreement on a £34m fee with Sassuolo for 23-year-old Bosnia international Tarik Muharemovic.

The Italian club had said earlier that talks were advancing for the centre back.

Juventus will receive 50percent of any fee so stand to receive £17m.

Tarik Muharemovic was on the end of this tackle from Folarin Balogun - for which the USA forward received a red card for but saw his ban suspended after Donald Trump intervened

Arsenal still in for Alvarez

Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez remains an option for Arsenal.

The Argentina forward would prefer to join Barcelona if they can reach agreement with Atletico but that relationship remains strained.

Arsenal are monitoring developments in case the opportunity to sign the 26-year-old opens up. Atletico have dismissed offers of £100m.

Two suitors for Rangers' Souttar

Leicester City and Sheffield United are showing interest in Rangers defender John Souttar.

The 29-year-old signed a new one-year deal at Rangers in February but did not travel to the club’s pre-season training camp in Spain, with Brazilian striker Danilo also staying at home.

John Souttar was one of three Rangers players at the World Cup with Scotland

Leeds want another keeper with Torino keen on Perri

Torino are pushing to sign Leeds United goalkeeper Lucas Perri but need the Elland Road side to sign another keeper first.

Leeds have seen out-of-contract Illan Meslier join Arsenal and Karl Darlow join Manchester United.

They have handed a new deal to Alex Cairns but are continuing to look for a new No1. Talks have taken place with Parma for Zion Suzuki but other options are also being explored.

Leeds remain in talks with Sassuolo over centre back Tarik Muharemovic and Southampton over Shea Charles. But, again, they have alternatives.

Tielemans proud to join United

Manchester United's midfield overhaul has moved on with the £35million signing of Youri Tielemans. The 29-year-old Belgian, who has joined from Aston Villa after his release clause was triggered, has signed a five-year deal at Old Trafford.

Tielemans said: 'It's hard to describe just how proud I am to join Manchester United.

'Signing for such a special club feels incredible, it is the culmination of years of dedication since I first fell in love with football.'

Click HERE to read more

Youri Tielemans has sealed his move to Old Trafford on a five-year deal

Arsenal ready for Tzolis bid after Trossard exit

Bruges are anticipating a bid from Arsenal for Christos Tzolis now that Leandro Trossard is confirmed as heading to Besiktas.

The Greece forward is keen on the move after seeing previous offers from the Premier League rejected, notably Crystal Palace.

The 24-year-old former Norwich winger also has interest from elsewhere but is set on Arsenal if they can agree a fee.

Christos Tzolis in action against Arsenal in last season's Champions League

Aberdeen head Feeney interest

Aberdeen head a list of clubs interested in Carlisle defender Morgan Feeney, 27, the club’s captain and player of the year signed by former boss Mark Hughes who has one year left on his contract.

The club’s American owners, who sacked Hughes, are yet to offer Feeney new terms.

JIM FOULERTON

Trossard completes £17m move to Turkey

Leandro Trossard has joined Besiktas from Arsenal in a deal worth £17million

Leandro Trossard has joined Besiktas from Arsenal in a deal worth £17m.

The Belgian winger departs the Premier League champions in a deal worth an initial £15.3m plus £1.7m in add-ons.

Trossard played a crucial role for Mikel Arteta playing 174 times in three-and-a-half years, scoring 36 goals.

During Arsenal's title-winning campaign last term, Trossard scored eight goals and registered 11 assists in 50 matches in all competitions.

Arsenal have been talking to Bruges over a deal for Christos Tzolis among other targets.

Leeds United are bringing in Cardiff City head analyst Matthew Jenkins who had been at the club for eight years.

City contemplating Bouaddi move

Manchester City are continuing to assess the figures being demanded by Lille for midfield prodigy Ayyoub Bouaddi.

As Daily Mail Sport have reported, City have retained a long-standing interest in the teenage Morocco international and want to bring in another midfielder alongside Elliot Anderson with long-term concerns over Rodri, who has still to agree a new contract.

Nico Gonzalez could be sold while Tijjani Reijnders, who had tentative interest from Atletico Madrid, could also go.

Bouaddi's performances have seen his value rise above £60m which was considered his asking price before the World Cup.

Manchester City have long held interest in Morocco star Ayyoub Bouaddi

Lille ideally wanted him to stay another season on loan as part of the deal but negotiations are open.

Meanwhile, Stade Brestois are among clubs showing interest in City defender Juma Bah who was on loan at Nice last season.

The 20-year-old, 6ft 5ins centre back could be among the players figuring in a showcase game at City today.

Darlow deal done

Manchester United have completed the signing of goalkeeper Karl Darlow.

The Wales international joins on a free transfer after his contract expired at Leeds.

Darlow finished last season as Leeds' number one and kept five clean sheets. They wanted to re-sign him while Everton and Tottenham also held talks.

Former Leeds goalkeeper Karl Darlow has made the move to Old rafford

Bristol City hope for Ballard compromise

Bristol City are working to find a compromise with Leyton Orient over a fee for striker Dom Ballard.

The 21-year-old, who scored 23 goals in League One last season, is set on a move to Ashton Gate but so far they have been unable to agree a deal with Orient who have been pushing for over £5million.

Southampton are also due sell-on percentage for the striker who, at the 2026 EFL Awards, was named in the League One Team of the Season, Player of the Season and Young Player of the Season.

Villa defender heading for Spain loan spell

Aston Villa right back Andres Garcia is closing on a loan move to Getafe.

The 23-year-old joined Villa from Levante 18 months ago in a £6million deal but made only 8 appearances last season.

Villa are looking to juggle a number of transfers this window to meet UEFA financial requirements.

They still want to strengthen after agreeing to sign Johan Manzambi from Freiburg but are losing Youri Tielemans to Manchester United for £36m and Lucas Digne to Paris St Germain for £8.5m.

There is also interest around Ollie Watkins and while they don't want to lose Morgan Rogers, offers from Arsenal are anticipated.

Sunderland land Thomas Menuier

Sunderland are signing Thomas Meunier on a two year contract.

The Belgium international, who was part of their World Cup squad, is a free agent after leaving Lille and has been talking to Valencia.

Hull City had also opened discussions with the 34-year-old right back but he has travelled to the North East this morning to complete a medical and sign for Sunderland.

Sunderland are signing Belgian international Thomas Meunier on a two year contract

Roma pressing for Garnacho

Roma are continuing to press for Chelsea misfit Alejandro Garnacho.

The Argentine has been granted permission to seek a new club and is not in Xabi Alonso's plans.

Chelsea want £40m and a permanent sale as Manchester United also retain a sell-on clause.

Roma are continuing to press for Chelsea misfit Alejandro Garnacho

Roma enquired a week ago and their latest proposal is for an initial loan with an option to buy for around £30m. It would become an obligation if certain conditions are met and the loan would carry a fee of £4.3m.

Chelsea maintain they want a guaranteed sale.

Chelsea are also looking to move on Axel Disasi, Benoit Badiashile and Filip Jorgensen. Mamadou Sarr could leave on loan amid Premier League interest.

Vuskovic leaves Spurs for Brighton

Luka Vuskovic has completed his move from Tottenham to Brighton for £46million plus £4m achievable add-ons.

Spurs have secured a 20 per cent sell-on clause for the Croatia international and buy-back matching rights.

Vuskovic and his representatives made clear his desire to play regular first team football in the season ahead and did not want another loan.

The 19-year-old centre half has had three separate loans since Spurs struck a deal to sign him from Hajduk Split for £12m.

Last season at Hamburg was a huge success but Roberto De Zerbi was unable to offer the guarantee of regular first team football at Spurs.

Luka Vuskovic has completed his move from Tottenham to Brighton for £46million plus £4m achievable add-ons

De Zerbi has reinforced in central defence with Marcos Senesi and Jan Paul van Hecke, who they signed from Brighton for £52m.

So, Spurs will bank a huge profit on a young player who never made a competitive appearance for them and whose wages they have never paid.

Only Harry Kane and Kyle Walker have been sold by Spurs for bigger fees in the last 10 years.

MATT BARLOW

Man City host showcase game for fringe stars

Manchester City host a showcase game today for the benefit of their fringe players.

Around 90 clubs are expected to be represented in the stands after they were invited to attend the game and view potential loan or permanent buy targets.

City players such as Preston North End target Divin Mubama, Matty Warhurst, Jaden Heskey, Claudio Echeverri, Spike Brits and Charlie Gray are all due to play a part as clubs from the UK and abroad come to take a close look.

A number of guest players from other clubs within City Football Group who are looking to move on have also been invited to take part. Stredair Appuah and Kris Lund from Palermo plus Amar Fatah and Elijah Odede from Troyes.

City have also scheduled a further showcase game against Salford City on August 4.

Sports.title: David Beckham has made thoughts clear on Diego Simeone after England vs Argentina controversy
Sports.content:
David Beckham has made thoughts clear on Diego Simeone after England vs Argentina controversy

Argentina midfielder Diego Simeone was at the centre of the David Beckham red card drama which contributed to England's World Cup exit in 1998

View Image David Beckham's red card against Argentina was one of the stories of the 1998 World Cup (Image: Bob Thomas Sports Photography via Getty Images)

Some 28 years on from England's controversial World Cup meeting with Argentina, the teams will meet again with a place in the final at stake. David Beckham and Diego Simeone have both been in attendance at their countries' matches after being the main characters in that 1998 meeting but their careers have long finished.

‌



It appears age has mellowed the former Three Lions star. Beckham was sent off for kicking out at Simeone in Saint-Etienne but seems to have buried the hatchet with his rival in the years since.

‌



England lost on penalties that night in France, though Beckham got some revenge four years later when his winner against the same opposition helped send England through from a 'Group of Death' while the South Americans were eliminated. More recently, though, Beckham and Simeone appear to be firm friends.

‌



After Argentina won the 2022 World Cup final, the Englishman shared a photo of the pair together with the caption "Congratulations my friend." Simeone re-posted the photo, adding his own caption: "Good to see you always!", while the bond still appears strong.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Beckham has strong Argentina connections through his Major League Soccer franchise Inter Miami. World Cup stars Lionel Messi and Rodrigo de Paul both play for the club, while 2014 World Cup finalist Gonzalo Higuain previously spent time on their books.

Argentina played their round of 32 match with Cape Verde in Miami and Beckham was joined by Simeone at the match. "Bumped into an old friend in Miami... @simeone," the former England star wrote while sharing a photo of the pair together on Instagram.

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Simeone also featured in Beckham's documentary for Netflix, which was released in 2023. The Englishman also shared his own reflections on the red card, admitting he still thought about it long after retiring.

“I made a stupid mistake. It changed my life. I felt very vulnerable and alone," he said. "I don't think I have ever talked about it just because I can't. I find it hard to talk through what I went through because it was so extreme. The whole country hated me. Hated me."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

He added: "I wasn’t eating. I wasn’t sleeping. I was a mess. I didn’t know what to do."

“It brought a lot of attention that I would never wish on anyone, let alone my parents," he adds. "I can’t forgive myself for that. That's the tough part what happened in a way. I was the one that made the mistake. It is only now I beat myself up about it."

Sports.title: Liverpool news: France World Cup transfer target emerges as fresh offer comes to light
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: France World Cup transfer target emerges as fresh offer comes to light

Liverpool's summer business could ramp up by the end of the week

View 3 Images Liverpool's transfer business could speed up after the World Cup (Image: LFCTV)

Liverpool's attention has turned to midfield in their aims to bolster their squad for Andoni Iraola. The Spaniard welcomed the return of several stars on Monday for pre-season with preparations for the 2026/27 season officially underway.

‌



Iraola, 43, has already overseen the arrival of new signings Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz, although the former's transfer was agreed when Arne Slot was at the helm. However, the Reds have yet to add to their squad since with a replacement for Mohamed Salah still yet to be secured.

‌



One area of focus for Iraola will be the Reds' midfield, which struggled significantly last season. Liverpool have been linked to a World Cup star while an offer that could result in the exit of one Anfield hero has come to light. Mirror Football takes a look at the latest transfer stories regarding the Reds.

‌



Chase for World Cup star

View 3 Images Manu Kone is reportedly back on Liverpool's radar (Image: getty images)

Liverpool's interest in Manu Kone has reportedly reignited years after first being linked to the Frenchman. The Roma star was first linked with a move to Anfield during Jurgen Klopp's tenure with reports surfacing again just a day after Andoni Iraola held his first press conference as Liverpool boss.

According to Italian outlet Corriere dello Sport, the Premier League giants want to add Kone - who is currently representing France at the World Cup - to their midfield with Roma under significant financial strain.

‌



The Serie A side are needing to raise £42million (€50m) in order to meet UEFA's financial fair play regulations. Kone was subject to interest from Atletico Madrid, who were said to be confident in securing a deal for the 25-year-old worth £38m (€45m).

However, Roma are now said to have raised the valuation of Kone to £51m (€60m) after UEFA extended their July 1 deadline by a month. Liverpool's midfield struggled heavily last season with Alexis Mac Allister and Ryan Gravenberch drastically dropping in form.

Curtis Jones update

Curtis Jones' future has been a question mark for much of the summer, as the 25-year-old has received plenty of interest from Inter Milan. The Serie A champions had a reported bid of £27m rejected for the midfielder last month, who is valued at £35m by the Reds.

‌



With summer business set to ramp up following the end of the World Cup on Sunday, Inter have sped up negotiations with a new approach made for Jones through intermediaries, according to Ben Jacobs.

View 3 Images Curtis Jones has 12 months left on his Liverpool contract (Image: Jacob King/PA Wire)

Amidst the uncertainty of his future, Iraola admitted he wants Jones to remain a Red this summer. Speaking on Monday, the Spaniard said: "I will have the chance to speak with him today.

‌



"I rate Curtis very highly. For me, he is a great, great player, and I hope he can continue with us and continue performing the way he has been performing. It's very important that he's Scouse, that he's from here.

"I also like the personality. From the outside, at least, he looks like a player with good character, and I hope we can keep him, not only for this year but for more time."

Sports.title: Alan Shearer has made thoughts clear on BBC future as Micah Richards announces plans to quit
Sports.content:
Alan Shearer has made thoughts clear on BBC future as Micah Richards announces plans to quit

Alan Shearer and Micah Richards have made their positions clear with regards to their media careers

View 2 Images Alan Shearer and Micah Richards have spoken about their futures in football media (Image: Jose Perez/Bauer-Griffin/GC Images)

Alan Shearer already stated he has no intention of leaving his BBC role amid Micah Richards’ bombshell announcement. Shearer and Richards both work for the BBC as football pundits, appearing on Match of the Day and currently covering the World Cup for the broadcaster.

‌



Richards, who is also a regular alongside Shearer on Gary Lineker’s The Rest Is Football podcast - the sixth-most popular podcast in the UK - has become one of the most recognisable faces in football media since retiring in 2019.

‌



The former England and Manchester City right-back, 38, also works for Sky Sports and CBS. But he recently announced his plans to step away from punditry by 2034.

‌



Richards pledged to quit in the next eight years in order to focus on community work in his hometown of Chapeltown, Leeds. But his colleague Shearer has no such plans to step away from his punditry and commentary duties just yet.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Micah Richards announces plan to quit BBC and Sky Sports READ MORE :

The Newcastle United legend, 55, saw his close friend Lineker leave the BBC last year after hosting Match of the Day for 26 years. In one episode of the flagship football highlights programme, Shearer was given the task of starting the show with a joke aimed at Lineker, who by then had already announced his impending departure.

‌



Later, when asked by Lineker about his new hosting duties on The Rest is Football, Shearer made his own position clear by saying: "No, I'm quite happy doing what I'm doing [punditry], so I'll leave that [presenting] to the experts."

View 2 Images Richards wants the World Cup 2034 to be his last punditry gig (Image: BBC)

Richards, however, has other plans. He told the Daily Telegraph this week: "I’ll be out of all this by the time I turn 46. You won’t see me on any mainstream media beyond the 2034 World Cup. That will be the last time I am on the BBC or Sky or CBS. I’ve told them all this and they think I’m joking. I’m not.

‌



"I’ve given so much of my life to football since leaving school at 14. But when the time comes, I want to make a difference to people’s lives at a grassroots level – to help those who need it most, especially young people.

"I come from Chapeltown in Leeds. It’s an area where there is so much talent, but a shortage of opportunity. I want to give something back. That’s my aim. I’ve no idea what form that will take, yet. There’s plenty of time to work that out.

"You see a lot of ex-footballers putting their names to foundations, which is great, but I want to do something more than giving money to charity or showing my face at an event once a year. Hopefully I can keep doing what I am doing for the next seven years – and just make sure I don’t get cancelled before then!"

Sports.title: Kylian Mbappe takes aim at Didier Deschamps and calls out France team-mates
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappe takes aim at Didier Deschamps and calls out France team-mates

Kylian Mbappe was speaking in the immediate aftermath of France's 2-0 World Cup semi-final defeat to Spain at Dallas Stadium on Tuesday night

View 2 Images Didier Deschamps and Kylian Mbbape after France were beaten 2-0 by Spain (Image: (Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto via Getty Images))

Kylian Mbappe took aim at Didier Deschamps' approach and tactics following France’s World Cup defeat to Spain. Mbappe saw his side’s hopes of reaching a third straight World Cup final end in Dallas after Mikel Oyarzabal and Pedro Porro scored to secure a 2-0 victory.

‌



The forward struggled to get into the game and his only chance of note saw him fire a free-kick harmlessly over. And the Real Madrid star seemed to question the way Deschamps set up his side when delivering his view on the game.

‌



He said: "We were three against two in midfield and against Spain, that's hard. Fabian [Ruiz] and Rodri had plenty of time to play.

‌



“There was a lack of communication on the press. I think we should have done man-to-man press and force them to run with us."

Before he added: "We didn't play the game we wanted, technically, tactically. When you don't do what you have to do in a World Cup semifinal, you don't win.

Didier Deschamps questions FIFA decision as France boss rages after Spain World Cup defeat READ MORE :

ITV presenter issues apology in parting dig to World Cup pundit ahead of final READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



“Spain respected their game plan and what the team usually does. They like to control the ball and the tempo. Our plan was to press them high so they could not install their rhythm.

"Because they are better than us at controlling a game. We didn't manage to do it. We were too sloppy technically. We could not hurt them when we could have.

"Even when we recovered the ball, our first touches were not good enough. That gives a defeat. It is a huge disappointment. But if we are objective, we didn't put all the ingredients to go to the final.”

‌



Despite the defeat, Mbappe’s team-mate Rayan Cherki claimed France are still 'better team' than Spain. He said:“They were better in every aspect of the game. “They wanted it more than we did. I am convinced that we are the better team, but this afternoon they were superior.

View 2 Images Kylian Mbappe during France's World Cup semi-final defeat to Norway (Image: ( Stefan Koops/EYE4IMAGES/NurPhoto via Getty Images))

“They did not apply excessive pressure, it wasn’t all over the pitch; there was time to play. Maybe we didn’t know how to control our emotions.”

‌



Before he added: “I don’t know if we lacked solutions or desire. Today, they recovered possession more easily than we did. If we had won back more balls, we would have hurt them more.

“At halftime, the coach told us there were still 50 minutes left and that we would have chances. The disappointment is enormous. We knew their main strength was playing at a slow pace. Sometimes, we should have done the same.

“It was more difficult than we expected. I tried to help push the comeback. I don’t think it was a lack of desire. They were better than us tactically, better positioned. We tried to solve those problems. We are in a World Cup semifinal; everything comes down to the details.”

Sports.title: Man Utd transfer news: Scott McTominay sent message as club hero set for emotional homecoming
Sports.content:
Man Utd transfer news: Scott McTominay sent message as club hero set for emotional homecoming

Manchester United's transfer window has sprung to life this week and it appears Michael Carrick's side aren't done yet

View 2 Images Andrey Santos was Manchester United's first summer signing (Image: Getty)

Manchester United have already confirmed the arrival of three summer signings. Youri Tielemans is the latest addition to Michael Carrick's squad.

‌



With Carrick at the helm, United will contest Champions League football next season and they've already begun strengthening their squad. Andrey Santos became their first signing of the window and his £50million move from Chelsea was confirmed on Monday.

‌



Karl Darlow has been snapped up after his contract with Leeds United expired. The signing of Tielemans from Aston Villa was also announced on Tuesday after the player's £35m release clause was activated.

‌



United are evidently focusing on rebuilding their midfield, something they may not have had to do if they hadn't offloaded the thriving Scott McTominay to Napoli. Now, the Scotsman has been sent a telling message by his new manager in Italy, as Mirror Football takes a look at the latest transfer news out of Old Trafford.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Ruben Amorim set to take advantage as Man Utd forced to cancel summer transfer READ MORE :

Scott McTominay message

Ever since signing for Napoli in 2024, McTominay has become one of Serie A's finest and his team's talisman. He led Scotland to the World Cup this summer, too, but failed to help them past the group stages.

‌



View 2 Images McTominay has a new manager (Image: Getty)

He is yet to return to Napoli following the tournament. Still, new manager Massimiliano Allegri has sent him and the rest of the players a telling message, perhaps hinting that if they don't adhere to his values, there could be issues.

"I learned from an old coach. Until I see and coach players, making judgments from outside is always very difficult. I'm taking it with me," said Allegri.

‌



"We'll get to know each other. Values are important. McTominay and [Noa] Lang will arrive before [August 5]. It will be important to work with seriousness and professionalism and above all, to lay the groundwork for reaching March. As I always say, that's when seasons are decided, still in contention for all our objectives: Serie A, the Champions League, the Italian Cup."

Club hero's homecoming

Another former United midfielder has completed an emotional transfer, as Ander Herrera returns to his boyhood club, Real Zaragoza, after leaving Boca Juniors in Argentina.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Herrera joined United in 2014 for £29m and made nearly 200 appearances for the club across five seasons. He contributed to FA Cup, Carabao Cup and Europa League wins before leaving in 2019 for Paris Saint-Germain.

More time with Athletic Bilbao followed before his stint in Argentina and he has now re-signed for Zaragoza on a one-year deal. He first joined the club aged 11.

Zaragoza's club website released a statement upon his arrival, which included the admission: "Ander's return is an unequivocal sign of belonging and represents the return of a Zaragoza native at a crucial moment for the club's future."

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham off-pitch life: Girlfriend with five-year age gap, £5m mansion, lives with mum
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham off-pitch life: Girlfriend with five-year age gap, £5m mansion, lives with mum

Jude Bellingham is England's main man hoping to lead the Three Lions to World Cup glory

View 4 Images England's World Cup hero Jude Bellingham with partner Ashlyn Castro (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

England will rely on Jude Bellingham to produce the goods again when they face Argentina in the World Cup semi-finals on Wednesday night. It will mark the biggest game of the 23-year-old superstar’s already glittering career.

‌



Bellingham, alongside Harry Kane, has been the Three Lions’ talisman throughout the tournament in the United States, Canada and Mexico, scoring six goals from midfield to put him in contention for the Golden Boot. Incredibly, he has scored a brace in each of England’s last two knockout games, which were both narrow wins over Mexico and Norway.

‌



But this is a player who has never been fazed by pressure throughout his career, from breaking onto the scene at Birmingham as a 16-year-old, to taking the Bundesliga by storm with Borussia Dortmund, and then spearheading a La Liga and Champions League double in his first season with Real Madrid.

‌



Expect Bellingham to step up and carry the nation's hopes on his shoulders once more when he comes up against Lionel Messi, the greatest footballer of all time. Now, beyond the on-pitch heroics and various high-profile brand endorsements, Mirror Football takes a look at Bellingham’s private life.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Harry Kane points the blame after Jude Bellingham and Thomas Tuchel disagreement READ MORE :

Girlfriend age gap

Bellingham’s romance with 28-year-old influencer Ashlyn Castro, five-and-a-half years his senior, reportedly began in 2024, when eagle-eyed fans noticed the pair exchanging likes and reacting to each other's social media posts. The relationship is said to have begun progressing in late 2024 before they were spotted on a lunch date together in Madrid in January 2025.

‌



Shortly afterwards, Castro was seen in Bellingham’s private box at the Bernabeu alongside his family during a Real Madrid match against Girona. They continued to appear together in public over the following months, including at the Madrid Open in April 2025, before going on holiday together off the coast of Sardinia.

View 4 Images Bellingham is in a relationship with influencer model Ashlyn Castro (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

‌



More recently, the Californian-born model has attended several of his World Cup 2026 matches in her home country. The pair were seen kissing after England’s opening fixture of the tournament - a 4-2 group stage win over Croatia.

As rumours linking her with Bellingham grew, Castro’s dating history came under scrutiny from fans online, having been linked with other celebrities such as Michael B. Jordan. She eventually took to TikTok last year to address the false rumours regarding her past. In the emotional video, the influencer clarified that she has only had three serious relationships over the last eight years, defending her personal life against disrespectful claims.

Long before finding herself in the spotlight, Castro built a successful career as a digital content creator and business owner. Amassing nearly one million followers across Instagram and TikTok, she has collaborated with major luxury beauty brands like Clarins, starred in the music video for DJ Khaled's 2021 hit song Popstar, and even founded her own talent representation agency, The Four Models.

‌



£5million mansion

View 4 Images Bellingham's dream home is located in Madrid (Image: Jude Bellingham/Youtube)

Whenever he wants some downtime away from his busy footballing schedule, Bellingham can kick back and enjoy his £5.5million mansion. His six-bedroom, 7,000 square-foot, luxury pad is located in the exclusive La Finca district in Madrid and boasts a swimming pool and a gym.

The start of the Real Madrid sensation’s love affair with his home was seen in the first episode of his 2024 YouTube series called 'Out of the Floodlights', which went behind the scenes of his life.

‌



The release of the inaugural episode, called 'Casa Blanca', saw Bellingham go house-hunting with his mum Denise, dad Mark and brother Jobe after his glamorous unveiling as Madrid's newest 'Galactico'. He was immediately enamoured with the property and had quite the smile on his face when trying the lift in what would become his future home.

His mum Denise referenced the intense Spanish heat, saying: "It’s extremely hot, he’s going to be sweltering." The large pool placed in the back garden provides the perfect relief for the searing summers in the European country.

Alongside the huge pool, Bellingham's property is said to also have the latest cutting-edge facilities including a home gym, home theatre, gourmet kitchen, private pool and stunning views of Lafinka Golf Club and mountain range.

‌



Living with mum

View 4 Images The Real Madrid sensation is very close with his parents (Image: JUSTIN TALLIS/AFP via Getty Images)

Despite being one of best footballers on the planet, Bellingham reportedly still lives with his mother. She originally moved to Spain when he signed for Los Blancos to provide a stable environment and help him behind-the-scenes.

Her role includes managing his daily schedule, financial affairs and routine logistics so he can focus on producing his best football. She also cooks his meals, with Bellingham stating upon his arrival in Madrid: "The role my mum is playing is massive. It is probably the biggest role of anyone, more than my coaches and managers, to be honest."

Article continues below

Denise made a similar move to Germany when he played for Borussia Dortmund. Meanwhile, his dad, Mark, stayed in England to support his younger footballer brother while he was at Birmingham and Sunderland.

Despite him now being 23, mother and son are believed to still share a living space that sums up their tight-knit family. Her key role was highlighted again recently by the midfielder after the dramatic 3-2 victory over Mexico, after which he noted how Denise repeatedly warned him to be careful about his behaviour, tackling and attitude during the game to avoid a yellow card, which would have meant missing out on the semi-final with suspension.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Julian Alvarez transfer timeline emerges as deal agreed for forward
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Julian Alvarez transfer timeline emerges as deal agreed for forward

Mikel Arteta is hoping to bolster his options during the summer transfer window ahead of the new season

View 3 Images Julian Alvarez is one of the big names who have been linked to Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal’s transfer business is finally beginning to gather pace after a sluggish start to the summer window. Fresh from ending their 22-year wait for a Premier League title, Mikel Arteta’s side have already strengthened with two new arrivals.

‌



Defender Piero Hincapie has completed a permanent £34.5million move from Bayer Leverkusen, while former Leeds United shot-stopper Ilan Meslier has joined on a free to bolster options in the goalkeeping department. But sporting director Andrea Berta is still determined to land a marquee signing as the Gunners look to retain their title and challenge for major honours on multiple fronts.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Arsenal have been linked with a string of elite names in recent weeks, including Morgan Rogers, Bruno Guimaraes and Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Jr. With Berta reportedly handed a transfer budget of around £250m, supporters are expecting several big moves before the deadline.

Mirror Sport takes a look at the latest transfer talking points from the Emirates Stadium

Julian Alvarez transfer timeline

England’s World Cup semi-final against Argentina on Wednesday evening is likely to have added significance for Arsenal’s hierarchy. One of the players expected to be on show is Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez, who has emerged as one of the Gunners’ top attacking targets.

‌



Arsenal dealt Bruno Guimaraes transfer blow as fans back Newcastle midfielder to stay READ MORE :

Gabriel Martinelli transfer odds shorten as Leandro Trossard Besiktas move confirmed READ MORE :

However, Arsenal may have to remain patient if they want to land the Argentine international – unless the Three Lions come out on top in Atalanta. According to Argentine newspaper La Nacion, Alvarez has no intention of deciding on his club future until after the World Cup has concluded, with the 26-year-old fully focused on representing his country.

The report claims Arsenal will step up their interest once the tournament finishes, when Alvarez will be “free to focus fully on his club future”. That could leave the Gunners facing a tight timeframe, with this summer’s expanded World Cup not wrapping up until July 19.

‌



View 3 Images Barcelona, Real Madrid and Arsenal have all been linked with Julian Alvarez (Image: Getty Images)

Barcelona reportedly remain Alvarez’s preferred destination, although the La Liga champions are struggling to agree a financial package with Atletico Madrid, who point to his whopping €500m (£426m) release clause. Argentine outlet Clarin Deportivo says Arsenal are “following every movement” and will advertise themselves as a serious alternative should Barcelona fail to agree a deal.

Deal agreed for forward

Leandro Trossard became a cult hero among the Gunners faithful during last season’s title-winning campaign, memorably scoring a crucial late winner against West Ham United in May. But the Belgian is set to bring his three-and-a-half-year spell in north London to an end this summer after Arsenal agreed a deal with Besiktas for the forward.

‌



View 3 Images Leandro Trossard of Arsenal celebrates scoring his team's first goal during the Premier League match between West Ham United and Arsenal at London Stadium (Image: Getty)

The 31-year-old has been granted permission to travel to Istanbul and complete a medical with the Turkish club ahead of a £17m move. Trossard departs having scored 36 goals in 174 appearances since joining from Brighton in January 2023.

His exit is expected to create room for Arsenal to recruit a new left-sided attacker, with Rogers and Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola among the names linked.

Sports.title: Didier Deschamps questions FIFA decision as France boss rages after Spain World Cup defeat
Sports.content:
Didier Deschamps questions FIFA decision as France boss rages after Spain World Cup defeat

Didier Deschamps failed in his attempt to win a second World Cup in charge of France, and he was not a happy man after his side's defeat to Spain

View Image Didier Deschamps following France's World Cup defeat to Spain (Image: (Alex Pantling - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images))

France boss Didier Deschamps questioned FIFA’s decision to appoint referee Ivan Barton for his side’s World Cup semi-final defeat to Spain. Goals from Mikel Oyarzabal and Pedro Porro secured Luis de la Fuente’s side a place in Sunday’s final against England or Argentina as Deschamps failed in his attempt to win a second World Cup as France boss.

However, the 57-year-old was left furious by Barton's decision to award a first-half penalty to Spain after Lucas Digne kicked Lamine Yamal when he attempted to clear the ball. He even asked reporters in his post-match conference if they felt Barton had the ability to handle a game of such stature.

“There is obviously a lot of disappointment,” Deschamps said. “The players are devastated because we had high ambitions.

“Although we have to be realistic and acknowledge that today we were a step below technically against a team that knew what they were doing. It’s primarily our fault.

“Then I ask a question, and I’m not going to answer it: 'Is the referee good enough to officiate a World Cup semi-final?'

ITV presenter issues apology in parting dig to World Cup pundit ahead of final READ MORE :

Ezri Konsa makes surprise admission over England preparations for Argentina clash READ MORE :

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

“We’ve had a few of those situations, and I’m not going to answer them. And I’m not saying this because we lost today, but there have been certain situations… often unfavourable to us, too.”

In a separate interview, Deschamps added: “I’m not going to dwell on it because otherwise I’ll sound like a crybaby. Is the referee up to the standard of officiating a World Cup semi-final? That’s for you to decide.

“I had fourth and fifth place referees next to me who were just as good. It’s not just the penalty, it’s a combination of factors. We’ve had more or less complicated situations in other matches. I have nothing against tonight’s referee, but ask yourselves the question.

“But the main reason is that we were a bit below par and less dangerous offensively than we could have been. We made a few technical errors and missed passes that could have led to situations and chances.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

“We have to accept it, this is the highest level, even if it hurts. It was the last step before this potential final… so we’ll play the third-place match. We’ll play it, it doesn’t take anything away from what we’ve achieved. But in this match, Spain showed something extra.”

Asked about Deschamps’ comments, Spain boss De la Fuente said: “Well, when things don’t go our way, we can always find some excuse. I have certainly had some difficult times with the refereeing, too.

“At times, it has reminded us of the match against Uruguay and I think that the referee’s leniency has something to do with it. I believe that you have to keep an eye on games and not let them get out of hand.

“But if that’s how it is, then we’ve both suffered. I don’t think at all that it was the complete opposite. In fact, they ruled out a goal and some very close situations, especially in some offside actions.

“But anyway, I’m not in a position to think about the referee right now. What I would like is for everyone to obviously improve, from referees to VAR to us, everyone who makes football, that we all become a little better every day.”

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
